original_test_intent: Measure approved sequential read and write performance on the owner-designated disposable HGX SSD/volume with NVQual Test #36 while proving error-free completion, device/filesystem health and host stability without hang or reboot.
original_method: Bind an expendable target by stable hardware/storage-stack identity and exclude protected storage; pin separate sequential read/write phases, access scope, block size, depth, workers, size, duration, direct-I/O/cache, preconditioning, repetitions and thresholds; preserve baselines; collect complete per-direction metrics, health, temperature and platform logs; stop on first target, media, filesystem or safety fault and restore only through the approved plan.
manual_activity: Owner designates the expendable target, approves data loss, sequential profile, thresholds and recovery; an operator verifies physical/logical identity and supervises re-provisioning.
required_inputs: Stable device serial/WWN/namespace and full storage-stack map
Disposable-target proof and explicit data-loss approval
Pinned Test #36/fio separate sequential read/write job with block size, depth, workers, size, duration, direct-I/O/cache, preconditioning and repetitions
Per-direction performance/latency/error/health/thermal limits, maintenance window, aborts and re-provision plan
safety_requirements: Never guess a storage target or use OS/boot/EFI/swap/LVM/RAID metadata/mounted production/unknown devices
Revalidate stable identity immediately before launch and inhibit on mapping change
Preserve logs and SMART/NVMe health before writes
Stop on wrong target, media/filesystem errors, unsafe temperature/power, capacity exhaustion, host instability, hang/reboot, tool failure or evidence gap
No automatic retry or unapproved repair
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only identity/stack/health validation against signed authorization
Run only the exact approved Test #36/sequential fio job
Collect complete separate read/write output, errors, health, temperature and logs
Stop/isolate on first fault; do not choose targets, repair/reformat, retry or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target/data loss, exact sequential phases, runtime and thresholds
Confirm exclusions, cache/direct-I/O semantics, preconditioning, monitoring and recovery
Review per-direction performance/health and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: fio is appropriate, but no command may be formed until target and sequential job are supplied; BW/IOPS alone omit latency, cache/direct-I/O effects, errors and health.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the pinned Test #36/fio job against the signed stable-identity disposable target with a launch-time identity interlock and complete machine-readable per-direction output plus health/log monitoring.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVQual Test #36, sequential SSD fio, all-items/no-hang/no-reboot Criteria, no bundle, and 5/60-minute allocation remain; missing target/profile values are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH DESTRUCTIVE SEQUENTIAL SSD TEST WITH TARGET IDENTITY INTERLOCK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed target/job manifest and independently measure sequential read and write phases under explicit cache/direct-I/O and preconditioning rules, with synchronized device/filesystem/thermal health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds protected-storage exclusions, stable identity, data-loss gate, direction-specific quantitative contract, launch interlock, health monitoring and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A combined fio summary can hide one weak direction, cache effects, wrong target, incomplete preconditioning or post-test device damage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sequential writes can erase data, consume endurance, overheat the device or fill a filesystem; reads can still expose latent media/controller faults and affect service.

project_override_considerations: File-backed and whole-device jobs have different destructive/performance coverage and must not be substituted silently. Buffered/cached results are not equivalent to direct media performance unless explicitly accepted.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, signed target authorization and data-loss approval
Stable serial/WWN/namespace/storage-stack map and protected-target exclusion proof
Pinned Test #36/fio job/config hash and direction-specific limits
Complete raw sequential read/write BW/IOPS/latency/error/runtime outputs and phase accounting
Pre/during/post SMART/NVMe health, media counters, temperature, filesystem/capacity, dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL
Abort/isolation/re-provision or clean final state and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Separates sequential read/write coverage, controls cache and preconditioning effects, and makes destructive stable-target authorization the launch interlock.
independent_technical_reasoning: Sequential performance is direction- and cache-sensitive. Buffered reads can measure RAM, while destructive writes depend on preconditioning and device steady state. Device paths are mutable, so the exact stable hardware and storage stack must be revalidated at launch. Each phase needs raw metrics and health evidence; rerunning after an anomaly risks data and causal evidence.
